title: Projects
description: Projects I build to explore ideas, solve frontend challenges and try new things.

mntn.title: MNTN
mntn.description: A responsive hiking-themed landing page built around scroll-driven storytelling, layered parallax and smooth motion. The project explores how animation and layout can work together without getting in the way of the content.

overview.title: Overview
paragraphs: MNTN is a portfolio landing page focused on motion, layered composition and scroll-based interaction.
The project explores how parallax, animated content sections and smooth scrolling can work together while keeping the content readable and the experience responsive across different screen sizes.

challenge.title: The challenge
paragraphs: The main challenge was coordinating multiple scroll-driven effects while keeping the layout responsive and the interaction smooth.

The hero is composed of several visual layers that move at different speeds, while content sections animate independently as they enter the viewport. This required careful control of positioning, animation timing and responsive behavior.

implementation.title: Implementation
paragraphs: Scroll-based animations are implemented with Motion, while Lenis is used to provide smooth scrolling throughout the page.
The application uses the Next.js App Router with localized routes powered by next-intl and theme switching handled with next-themes.
The codebase follows a feature-oriented architecture that separates page composition, larger UI sections, user interactions and reusable shared components.

coffee.title: Bean Scene
coffee.description: A responsive coffee shop landing page with an interactive menu, drink customization, and a shopping cart. In this project, I focused on creating an intuitive ordering flow, from choosing drink sizes and quantities to editing the cart and confirming an order.

overview.title: Overview
paragraphs: Bean Scene is a fictional coffee shop landing page that combines brand presentation, a drinks menu, and a client-side ordering flow.
In this project, I explored how to extend a promotional page with interactive features while maintaining clear navigation, responsive layouts, and an accessible interface.

challenge.title: Challenge
paragraphs: The main challenge was keeping cart state, drink customization, and price calculations in sync so that every user action was consistently reflected in the interface.
This required handling identical drinks of the same size, quantity limits, and the empty-cart state. Dialogs, notifications, and keyboard interactions also needed careful attention to accessibility.

features.title: Key Features
items: Drink size and quantity selection in a dialog
Dynamic drink pricing and order-total calculation
Shopping cart with quantity controls and item removal
Automatic merging of identical drinks of the same size
Order confirmation that clears the cart
Notifications with an action to open the cart
Feedback carousel and scroll-triggered section animations
Optimized WebP images with lazy loading

implementation.title: Implementation
paragraphs: The project is built with semantic HTML, CSS, and TypeScript using Vite. The main content and menu are available in the HTML, while interactive flows are implemented in separate TypeScript modules.

Cart state management is separated from rendering and event handling. The drinks catalog and base prices are centralized, while pricing calculations and quantity limits are handled in a dedicated module.

Dialogs use the native HTML dialog element, section reveal animations use IntersectionObserver, and feedback transitions use the Web Animations API. Dynamic updates include screen reader announcements, and animations respect the prefers-reduced-motion setting.
